_doc: InvisiSpec transmission criterion: a footprint of an unsafe speculative load in any protected data-cache-hierarchy structure, observed in the O3PipeView trace only (SimSpect hook lines, wiki/design/SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md). Evaluated by STAGE3_gem5/check_footprint.py. Format: wiki/design/TRANSMISSION_CRITERIA_FORMAT.md. Scope quotes re-checked against the audit (wiki/findings/mdsToRead/FOOTPRINT_DEFENSES_PAPER_AUDIT.md §2, §7) and the PDF text.
status: v1 2026-10-28 (criteria session); scope = Anna's 2026-10-28 decision (everything the paper protects).

requires.why: the InvisiSpec cache defense is Ruby-only; classic --caches runs do not exercise it (audit finding 1)

claims.quote: InvisiSpec blocks covert and side channels that are constructed by monitoring the state of any level of a multiprocessor data cache hierarchy. This includes cache state such as occupancy (e.g., what lines live in what sets), replacement information, and coherence information (e.g., whether a line is in the Exclusive or Shared state). It also includes data TLB state (e.g., what entries live in the TLB).
claims.supports: observation.structures (L1D, L2=LLC, DIR, DTLB) + observation.state (presence, replacement, coherence)

claims.quote: USLs do not modify the cache coherence states, cache replacement algorithm states, or any other cache hierarchy state.
a Spec-GetS obtains the line from the directory … without changing any cache or coherence states
To prevent a USL from observably changing the D-TLB state … on a D-TLB miss, it delays serving it via a page table walk until the USL reaches the point of visibility
[the validation/exposure at the visibility point] will make all the side effects of the USL in the memory hierarchy apparent
claims.supports: observation.allowed: footprint at/after expose/validate is legal (Futuristic actor)

claims.quote: In the Spectre attack model, USLs are the speculative loads that follow an unresolved control-flow instruction. As soon as the control-flow instruction resolves, the USLs that follow it in the correct path of the branch transition to safe loads

In our Futuristic attack model, USLs are all the speculative loads that can be squashed by an earlier instruction. A USL transitions to a safe load as soon as it becomes either (i) non-speculative because it reaches the head of the ROB or (ii) speculative non-squashable by any earlier instruction

In our defense against Futuristic attacks, a USL reaches its visibility point only when: (i) it is not speculative anymore because it is at the head of the ROB, or (ii) it is still speculative but cannot be squashed anymore. At that point, the hardware issues a validation or an exposure for the load
claims.supports: actors.modes.futuristic.vp = first expose/validate of i, or i reaching the ROB head

granularity.DTLB: page (TLB events carry the virtual page, SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md)

observation.notes: L2 is the LLC in our 2-level Ruby runs. SB/LLCSB are InvisiSpec's own buffers (allowed). MSHR/TBE buffers are ignored: MSHR contention is out of scope (below).

spec.text: squashed(i) ∧ lc_seq < i.seq  (pinned 2026-10-28: what the tests realize; i = the event's seq joined to the O3PipeView fetch seqNum; squashed = never retired and younger than a ROB:squash seq while allocated before that squash)

futuristic.text: footprint e by instruction i (e.seq) with e.tick < vp(i), vp(i) = min(first L1D expose|validate tick with seq=i, rob_head(i)); rob_head(i) = latest retire tick among retired instructions older than i (i retired), else ∞. Any instruction counts (Futuristic USL = every squashable load), committed or squashed.
futuristic.limit: condition (ii) 'speculative non-squashable' is visible only through the expose/validate it triggers; a load that became non-squashable before it issued (so issued as a normal load, no expose) would be flagged. Triage via vp_basis in the record.

footprint.text: lc_retire < e.tick < fnc_retire (fnc_retire==0 → ∞; no lc annotated → no lower bound) ∧ every annotated unresolved branch still unresolved at e.tick (gem5_common.check_branch_resolutions), same window as check_ld.py

leak.text: leak ⇔ ∃ e ∈ E({fill, evict, inv, coh, repl_touch}, OBS) : actor(e.seq, e) ∧ e ∈ window(actor mode)

not_covered.item: in-flight squashed loads with no O3PipeView fetch record
not_covered.why: their seq still joins (squash status is inferred from ROB:squash + seq order), but pc/stage ticks are unavailable (SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md gaps)
seq comes from a per-line most-recent-cause map, not per message (SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md); a footprint attributed this way is reported with its struct so triage can discount it

not_covered.item: coherence effects on a remote core (CrossCore setting)
not_covered.why: single-core SE runs; only this core's own DIR/L2 coh transitions are observable

out_of_scope.note: scoping problem of the defense, not an implementation bug we catch

claim.quote: For simplicity, we do not describe the protection of the instruction cache or instruction TLB. However, we believe they can be protected with similar or even simpler structures.

out_of_scope.note: scoping problem of the defense, not an implementation bug we catch

claim.quote: contention on other resources, such as MSHRs or execution units, could slow down the receiver, but such side channels are considered out of scope in this paper (Section III-B).

out_of_scope.item: execution units, NoC, DRAM contention, fine-grain SMT structures, physical (power/EM) channels
out_of_scope.note: scoping problem of the defense, not an implementation bug we catch
